name: MIPLIB 2017 open instance gmut-76-50
description: Find a feasible solution of the MIPLIB 2017 instance gmut-76-50 with as low an objective value as possible (a maximisation model is negated, so that lower is better for every instance). A solution is feasible when every variable bound, every row bound and the integrality of every integer variable hold within an absolute tolerance of 1e-6 on the values as they are returned; integer variables are not rounded first.

sources.locator: A cutting plane method for solving harvest scheduling models with area restrictions
Harvest Scheduling Subject to Maximum Area Restrictions: Exploring Exact Approaches
Gleixner et al. (2021), MIPLIB 2017: data-driven compilation of the 6th mixed-integer programming library (benchmark paper, not evidence).
Instance pages with submitter, group, status and best known objective.

execution.interface: solve(model) -> numpy array of num_cols values, one per column. model has name, mps_path (the uncompressed MPS file), num_cols, num_rows, A (scipy CSR matrix of the rows), col_cost, col_lower, col_upper, row_lower, row_upper, integrality (bool array), offset, maximise and indicators (a list of (row, column, value): such a row has to hold only when that column equals the value; empty for most instances). Score: col_cost @ x + offset in minimisation form (negated when maximise is true), minimized; an infeasible vector is invalid.

limitations: The objective listed on the open-instances page may have been improved since 2026-11-11 (the list did not change between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-11).
Candidates may call HiGHS through highspy; a stronger solver is a method, not a discovery by the workflow.
The record was found in a hashed snapshot of its source; it is not replayed. See VALIDITY.md.

notes: our verifier does not accept the published solution: an integer variable is not integral (largest violations: rows 7.8e-10, bounds 0.0e+00, integrality 9.5e-06). MIPLIB's own check is looser than this task's absolute 1e-6, so matching the record here needs a cleaner solution; a result that beats it here also beats it there

Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
science_relevance.reason: Both papers have harvest scheduling with maximum clearcut area restrictions as their main objective, the model described on the MIPLIB page.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Choose which management units (and generalised units) to harvest in which period to maximise net timber revenue subject to single harvest, harvest-flow, minimum final average age and maximum clearcut size constraints (instance gmut-76-50).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Maximum clearcut size limits are a regulatory requirement in forestry; including them makes harvest planning a hard combinatorial problem.
